request_messages.content:
You evaluate generated software tests against one payments specification.
Return one JSON object and no other text. Do not use Markdown.
Use only the supplied requirement IDs and test IDs.
Every test must contain every requirement exactly once.
Status must be one of: covered, partial, missing, incorrect, not_applicable.
Scores must be numbers from 0 to 10.
Evidence must be an exact short quote from that test. If you cannot quote it, do not use covered.
The artifact contains only a description, steps, and expected result. Do not penalize it for omitting executable code.
Use not_applicable when the test does not attempt the requirement.
Use incorrect when the test asserts behavior that conflicts with the specification.
Use partial when the test mentions the requirement but would not prove it.

We need to produce JSON with evaluations for each test case. Must include every requirement exactly once per test. So for each test case, we need an array of requirement assessments covering all 8 requirements. For each requirement, we must set status (covered, partial, missing, incorrect, not_applicable). Provide evidence (exact quote from the test). If cannot quote, do not use covered. Provide reasoning one sentence.

Also need correctness_score and bug_detection_score numbers 0-10, plus reasoning sentences, and risks array.

We must follow response_schema: evaluations is list of objects each with test_case_id, requirement_assessments (list), correctness_score, bug_detection_score, correctness_reasoning, bug_detection_reasoning, risks.

We have 4 test cases. For each, we must assess each of the 8 requirements.

We must consider the test content.

Test tc-1: description "Verify that a wallet top-up completes successfully". Steps: "Initiate top-up of SGD 500", "Check wallet balance increases". ExpectedResult: "Wallet balance increases by SGD 500". This test only checks balance increase, not FX lock, credit before debit, timeout, rollback, approval. So for many requirements, status will be missing or not_applicable? The rule: Use not_applicable when the test does not attempt the requirement. So for each requirement not attempted, we should use not_applicable. For those attempted but not fully proven, maybe partial. For tc-1, it attempts credit-before-debit? It checks wallet balance increase, but does not verify order of credit vs debit. So it mentions credit but not order. So status maybe partial? But rule: "Credit before debit requires that order, not merely a balance increase." Since test only checks balance increase, it does not verify order, so it's not covering requirement. It attempts maybe but insufficient, so partial? The spec says status must be one of covered, partial, missing, incorrect, not_applicable. Since test mentions balance increase, it attempts requirement but does not prove order, so partial. However "missing" could be used when test does not attempt requirement at all. Since it attempts credit (balance increase) but not order, it's partial. For other requirements not mentioned, use not_applicable.

But we must include each requirement exactly once per test. So for each requirement we must assign a status. For those not attempted, not_applicable.

ExpectedResult: "FX rate matches rate locked at initiation". This attempts fx-lock requirement. It mentions "FX rate shown equals rate at initiation time". That is coverage of fx-lock. Does it also cover credit-before-debit? No. So status for fx-lock: covered (has exact quote). Provide evidence: "Check that FX rate shown equals rate at initiation time". For other requirements, not_applicable.

Test tc-3: "Verify rollback on timeout". Steps: "Initiate top-up", "Simulate provider timeout", "Check wallet balance". ExpectedResult: "Wallet balance unchanged and funding source not debited". This attempts timeout-after-5s? It mentions simulate provider timeout but does not specify 5 seconds. Rule: "Timeout coverage requires the five-second boundary, not the word timeout alone." Since test does not mention 5 seconds, status for timeout-after-5s is partial? Actually it attempts but not specific, so partial. For rollback-on-timeout: test verifies rollback on timeout, so covered? It says "Verify rollback on timeout" and expected result includes wallet unchanged and funding source not debited. That covers both rollback and neither side affected. But need to separate: rollback-on-timeout requirement: "A timed-out provider callback rolls the transaction back." The test verifies rollback, so covered. Provide evidence: "Simulate provider timeout". Might be considered coverage. For neither-side-affected: also covered by expected result "Wallet balance unchanged and funding source not debited". Provide evidence: "Wallet balance unchanged and funding source not debited". For credit-before-debit: not attempted. Not_applicable. For fx-lock: not attempted. Not_applicable. For approval requirements: not applicable.

Test tc-4: "Verify large top-up requires approval". Steps: "Initiate top-up of SGD 15,000", "Check approval screen appears". ExpectedResult: "Approval screen is shown". This attempts approval-above-10000, second-owner-approval, no-settle-before-approval. It checks approval screen appears, but does not verify second owner or that settlement is blocked. So status: approval-above-10000: covered? It checks that approval screen appears for >10000, so covered. Provide evidence: "Check approval screen appears". second-owner-approval: not verified, only approval screen, not who approves. So partial? It mentions approval but not second owner. So partial. no-settle-before-approval: not verified, no settlement check. So missing or not_applicable? It attempts requirement (top-up requires approval) but does not verify settlement blocked, so partial? The rule: "Approval coverage requires the above-SGD-10000 boundary, the second owner, and blocked settlement." Since test only covers boundary and screen, not second owner or blocked settlement, overall requirement not fully covered. For each sub-requirement we assess individually. For no-settle-before-approval, test does not attempt settlement, so missing? It doesn't attempt to verify settlement, so missing. Use not_applicable? The test does not attempt settlement, but the requirement is about settlement. Since test does not attempt, not_applicable. But we need each requirement exactly once; we can assign not_applicable for those not attempted. For no-settle-before-approval, test does not attempt settlement, so not_applicable.

Now we need to compute correctness_score and bug_detection_score for each test. The scores are numbers 0-10. We need to give reasoning one sentence each. We need to evaluate based on behavior the test attempts. Since we don't have actual test execution, we can assign generic scores. Probably low scores because tests are incomplete. Provide some reasoning.
